newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk Nadezhdinsky workers may not strike-source.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk Nadezhdinsky workers may not strike-source.

text.p: An official at the Nadezhdinsky metallurgical plant, part of the Norilsk Nickel NKEL.RTS group's main combine, said on Tuesday that he did not think Nadezhdinsky workers would join any strikes.
"Our mood is a bit calmer," said the official, in the plant's economics department, who did not identify himself.
"It's not in our interest to stop output. We believe the promises (that arrears will be repaid)," he said.
About 10,000 Nadezhdinsky workers disrupted nickel and copper output in early June 1996 over living conditions and wage arrears.
Nadezhdinsky accounts for about 25 percent of the Norilsk Nickel group's (RAO Norilsky Nickel) 0#NKEL.RUO total output.

Valery Glazkov, head of the Norilsk main plant's United Trade Union, said on Tuesday that workers at the Norilsk NKEL.RTS flagship metals plant, of which Nadezhdinsky is part, planned a warning strike March 27 and a proper strike April 2.
Glazkov said that the 60 units of the main Norilsk plant, known as the mining and metallurgical complex, would decide for themselves how to disrupt output.
